chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) passed by me while I was walking alongside my she-camel. He said: 'What is the matter — why are you not riding?' I said: 'My she-camel has weakened, and I wanted to lighten the burden on her.' He said: 'May God have mercy on you! Ride, for God carries the burden of both the weak and the strong.'

key_terms.نَاقَة: She-camel; in the context of early Islamic travel, camels were primary means of long-distance transport and had legal and ethical norms governing their treatment.
key_terms.يَحْمِلُ: Carries/bears; used here in the sense of God undertaking a burden — a theological reassurance that relying on one's mount does not oppress the animal when God sustains all.

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about riding a weakened camel and God's mercy?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) encounters his companion Abdallah ibn Abi Ya'fur walking beside his weakened she-camel out of compassion for the animal. The Imam corrects this behavior with a blessing and a theological principle: God bears the weight of both the weak and the strong, meaning one need not refuse a lawful convenience on the basis of misplaced mercy. The teaching reflects the Imam's pastoral role in guiding practical conduct through theological insight.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on you
